payload.text: The ▇▇▇ is a toothed whale of the Arctic, the only member of its genus and one of two survivors of its family. It is stocky, with a blunt snout, a large rounded melon and a low ridge where other whales carry a fin. The male grows a straight spiralled tusk of one and a half to three metres, which is really a left canine tooth pushing through the lip; it may serve for feeding, for courtship, or for tasting how salty the water is. These animals live off Canada, Greenland and Russia, and each year they move to shallow ice-free grounds, often the same ones. Diving as deep as 2,370 metres, the ▇▇▇ is among the deepest divers of all.

reveal.subject: Narwhal

sources.excerpt: The narwhal (Monodon monoceros) is a species of toothed whale native to the Arctic. It is the only member of the genus Monodon and one of two living representatives of the family Monodontidae. The narwhal is a stocky cetacean with a relatively blunt snout, a large melon, and a shallow ridge in place of a dorsal fin.

Males of this species have a spiralled tusk that is 1.5–3.0 m (4.9–9.8 ft) long, which is a protruding left canine thought to function as a weapon, a tool for feeding, in attracting mates or sensing water salinity.

Narwhals inhabit the Arctic waters of Canada, Greenland and Russia. Every year, they migrate to ice-free summering grounds, usually in shallow waters, and often return to the same sites in subsequent years.
Diving to depths of up to 2,370 m (7,780 ft), the narwhal is among the deepest-diving cetaceans.
